items.text: Hey everyone!
A new patch for Desolatium has been updated on Steam, check out the fixes:
🗡️ Achievement “Life, death and madness” could not be unlocked
🗡️ Users were able to launch multiple instances of the game
🗡️ Typo in the Spanish city sign “La Ciudad sin Nombre”
Greeting cultists!
We start the weekend with good news: New Desolatium Demo patch is now live!
While we continue with the development of Desolatium, we have taken the time to make some improvements to the current demo: so update the game for the following
We have replaced one of the NPCs with the definitive one.
We have added the option to adjust the volume (music and voices), plus some new sounds.
Fixed some transitions
We have better integrated some notes in the scenes.
You can check some of the improvements in our March devlog or by playing the demo (we recommend the second option ːsteammockingː).

We want to hear your feedback, so please use the Steam comments to leave your impressions and help us improve the final game. Until then, we will keep working and praying to the Dark and Primeval Gods.

"But remember that dark world of fungoid gardens and windowless cities isn't really terrible. It is only to us that it would seem so. Probably this world seemed just as terrible to the beings when they first explored it in the primal age. You know they were here long before the fabulous epoch of Cthulhu was over, and remember all about sunken R'lyeh when it was above the waters”
The Whisperer In Darkness, The Haunter Of The Dark – H. P. Lovecraft
Greeting cultists!
As every month, here is our devlog! A way to bring you closer to the development of Desolatium.
March has been great! We have made great progress in the development and we will show you some things to highlight from this past moth:

Some of the scenes were missing, such as the secret Theron Marks Society room. We still hadn’t found the perfect scenario for that location, but we finally did in Toledo, a small town close to Madrid, 4 hours away from our living city.
Fun fact: we finally got to meet Isabel, the only one in our team who works remotely in another city: The one in charge of the Art in Desolatium!
Here are some of the behind the scenes pics! (You will love this scene in the game, specially when you see the transformation)
We keep working on the detail views of the things you will need to find: notes, objets, clues… Here’s one of them: a drawer with a note and an old book inside. What will they be needed for?
We have also colour-graded and edited more images, like this street:
And added some elements to other images. We needed more chaos so we added some books and blood in this library:
As we told you last month, we have been working on a new update of the demo, these are some of the changes you will be able to see:
Idd Yahh wasn’t ready when we released the demo, but she is now! So we have replaced her in the scene:
Here you will be able to control the music and sound effects, one of the things we have been asked for the most!
You will have to play to discover the rest of the improvements, but we will tell you more about it in our next post here in Steam, so stay tuned!!
And that wraps it up! Make sure that you're up to date by following our socials for Desolatium related news! Check out our links here:
Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, Discord
We would be so grateful if you would also wishlist us on steam if you haven't already!

releases.displayName: Dev live stream and new demo update for Steam Next Fest!

items.text: Dear cultists,

As we told you in our last post, we’re happy to see that many of you have played and enjoyed the Desolatium demo. We’ve been watching you on Youtube and Twitch, hearing your suggestions and reading your comments and we have some good news: we will release another demo update soon.
We’ve fixed some bugs and added features and tweaks that were suggested by those of you who gave the demo a try:
Fixed some transitions between screens
Added some sounds (such as steps or door sounds) and replaced others.
Better integrated notes on the scene
Fixed some sounds and voices: now you can adjuste the volumen!
There are a few more small changes, but these are the highlights. Thank you for all of your feedback, it’s been invaluable!

We will tell you more about the new updates in our live stream for Steam Next Fest friday 7pm CEST. But we won't be alone! Raziel317 will join us! He will be commenting, chatting with us, and asking some interesting things about the game. See you there?
Make sure that you're up to date by following our socials fore Desolatium related news! Check out our links here:
Twitter | Facebook | Instagram | Discord
We would be so grateful if you would also wishlist us on steam if you haven't already!
Greetings Cultists!
Here is our monthly update to provide you with inside information on what has been happening in the development of Desolatium!

January has been a crazy month! We’ve been a part of The Big Adventure Event and many streamers and people played and tested the demo. They have given us a lot of feedback to implement in the development in order to improve the experience, so we have focused on that.
Apart from it, our great artist, programmer and creative devs continued non-stop with the game development of Desolatium. Here are the main things to highlight from this first month of the year:
We’ve finished all the graphic material from chapters 4, 5 and 6: notes, titles, descriptions, objetcs…
Also some of the 3D objects from chapter 6 have been made, meet this Dagon!
Color grading all chapter 6 images.

Mask men is finally ready! Here is the concept art vs 3D.: And that wraps it up! Many more things have been done but we don't want to reveal everything now ːsteammockingː: Make sure that you're up to date by following our socials fore Desolatium related news! Check out our links here: Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, Discord: We would be so grateful if you would also wishlist us on steam if you haven't already!
Hello cultists!
A few months ago we came up with the idea of making a shorter game, while we keep developing DESOLATIUM, in order to make the wait more bearable. And this is how DESOLATIUM: PROLOGUE was born.
It was at first published on Steam for our backers to try it and thanks to their feedback, we developed a new and improved version.
We have always believed that God sent his son into the world to save us. But, what if that is not what happened? What if the world cannot be saved? The real story is about to be revealed.

You will explore a city outside the limits of time and space; meet mysterious characters who will guide you on your journey; interact with the objects around you to solve complex puzzles in order to get to the terrible presence of a cosmic entity of immense power: Cthulhu.
The time has come to answer the call of The Great Dreamer.
Hyper-realistic graphics: All levels have been generated by shooting real locations in 360º and the integration of 3D elements in post-production.
Graphic point & click adventure full of mystery.
Ambisonic Audio (8D): It generates an immersive sound effect that seems to come from all around the player. You will only need your headphones to live this experience.
Full immersion: Desolatium: Prologue is available for PC/MAc and, if you want to achieve total immersion, you are able to use a Virtual Reality device (Steam and Oculus).
Inventory: You will be able to combine objects in order to create new ones.
Dialogue: From now on, you will have the possibility to talk with other characters.
Cinematic scene: Made using motion graphics.
Design: New designs for the game interface that will immerse you even more in the adventure.
New enemies with new animations.
Puzzles: more complex riddles you will have to solve.
Lore: Many more references, both to the universe created by Lovecraft and to other horror classics.
Music and effects: The experience will be improved thanks to the great Xabi San Martín, who has created new melodies for this prologue.
DESOLATIUM: PROLOGUE ON STEAM: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1640540/Desolatium_Prologue/
